events.summary: Surgery always carries some level of risk, and not every unexpected outcome is the result of negligence. However, when a healthcare professional fails to meet the accepted standard of medical care and that failure causes avoidable harm, the situation may amount to Surgical Negligence. Determining the difference often requires a careful review of medical records, expert opinions, and the circumstances surrounding the procedure. Warning signs can include operating on the wrong site, delayed treatment of complications, retained surgical instruments, anesthesia errors, or inadequate post-operative care. It is also important to consider whether the patient was properly informed of the risks before consenting to surgery. Establishing negligence involves proving that the injury was preventable and directly caused by substandard care rather than an unavoidable complication. Because these cases can be medically and legally complex, professional legal guidance is essential. Ciano Carroll Solicitors represents individuals who believe they have suffered avoidable harm due to medical errors and helps them understand whether they may have a valid claim. Their experience in handling complex medical negligence matters enables clients to navigate the legal process with confidence. By working with independent medical experts and thoroughly investigating each case, the firm evaluates whether the required legal standard for negligence has been met. Anyone concerned about the outcome of a surgical procedure should seek advice as early as possible to protect their legal rights. Understanding the distinction between an accepted surgical risk and Surgical Negligence is the first step toward determining whether compensation may be available.
events.title: How can you tell if a surgical complication was actually negligence?

events.summary: The Multnomah Arts Center (MAC) in Portland, Oregon will open two new exhibitions in its Front and Center Galleries this August. tende·r·eprisal // futu·re·prise, a group exhibition of bronze works created by multiple artists through a collaborative process led by elijah jamal asani, will be featured in the Front Gallery. In the Center Gallery, large-scale wood sculptures by Philip A. Robinson Jr. will be paired with functional and sculptural ceramic works by Swapna Mukhopadhyay. Both exhibitions run August 7–September 12, 2026, with a joint reception on Thursday, August 20, from 6 to 8 p.m. elijah jamal asani, a Nigerian-American artist, convened an intergenerational group of regional Black artists to create a collection of contemporary bronze artifacts. Their work was made in response to the historic theft of the Benin Bronzes. “Dating back to the 13th century, artists from the Kingdom of Benin, which is in modern-day southern Nigeria, cast bronze into sacred altar pieces and vessels of ancestral memory,” says asani. “However, in 1897, thousands of these bronze artifacts were looted by British forces.” They have yet to be repatriated. As an act of “selfdetermined restitution,” asani worked with other Black artists to create new bronzes. MAC is honored to exhibit eleven of these sculptures, created by Adriene Cruz, Midnite Seed Abioto, Intisar Abioto, Hanifah Abioto, Vaughn Kimmons, Turiya Raiah, Nyasiah Calixte, Lea Dry, Hannah Dry, Nawens Dry, and elijah jamal asani. Swapna Mukhopadhyay creates functional and sculptural porcelain works, all hand built. “The combination of aesthetics and functionality in handmade folk artifacts has always fascinated me,” she says. “My grandmother made traditional Bengali quilts (kanthas) and wove mats for sitting on the floor (asanas). I now realize how deeply I was influenced by watching her work.” Delicate drawn elements adorn many of her ceramic surfaces, and several recent works incorporate textiles and found objects. Mukhopadhyay describes her process as “improvising around what’s available,” informed by her longtime study of ethnomathematics. A retired PSU professor, she sees mathematics as inherent to creative practice and creative expression as integral to daily life across many cultures. Her ceramic pieces are often small in scale and characterized by what she calls their “putting togetherness.” Philip A. Robinson Jr. is a sculptor and conceptual artist whose work has been exhibited nationally and internationally. Working primarily in wood and metal, Robinson creates large-scale figurative and patterned works that explore memory, structure, and identity. “My practice examines structure as a living system—how materials carry memory, how patterns encode history, and how built environments shape identity,” he explains. “Whether in wood or steel, I am asking how structure holds memory—and how we locate ourselves within it.” The exhibition will include pieces from several bodies of work, including a 42” x 61” sculpture from Welcome In, which examines belonging, and several works from The House of Regina, which honor the legacy of his late mother, Dr. Regina Arnold. Robinson holds a BFA in Studio Art from Skidmore College and an MFA in Sculpture from the Mason Gross School of the Arts at Rutgers University. The Multnomah Arts Center is located at 7688 SW Capitol Hwy, Portland, OR, 97219. It is open Monday – Thursday 9 a.m. to 9:30 p.m., and Friday – Saturday 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. The galleries are free and open to the public during these hours. Additional Information: The Multnomah Arts Center is a part of Portland Parks & Recreation. MAC offers programs in a wide range of visual, music, movement, theater, and literary arts at an affordable cost to people of all ages. In addition to this vibrant arts education program, MAC runs a community-based visual arts exhibition program, which includes the MAC Front & Center Galleries. MAC also hosts theatre, music and dance performances, and other special events. The Multnomah Arts Center Association (MACA) is an all-volunteer, 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization that exists to support equity and access to arts education at MAC. MACA provides scholarships, supports community engagements efforts, and provides specialized arts equipment and facility improvements. Their efforts expand opportunities and enhance the experience of students, instructors, and the community at-large. For more information about MAC or MACA, please call 503.823.2787 or visit www.multnomahartscenter.org

events.summary: PDX CONTEMPORARY ART is pleased to present THE HEROINES, a new exhibition by Seattle-based artist Victoria Haven. For this body of work, Victoria Haven referenced The Heroides, a collection of poems by Ovid written from the perspective of fifteen heroines of Greek and Roman mythology. Using the poems as source material and framework, the works in the exhibition dissect and reassemble mythological narratives into an invented language. The Heroines Alphabet, a series of graphite drawings, uses the title of the show as a system for revealing hidden words. Placed in a grid, Haven connects adjacent letters in ‘The Heroines’ to form new words, some with multiple readings or meanings. The Linguistic Architecture drawings abstract the alphabet further, transforming each letter of the title phrase into dark, inky rectangles with bright scarlet notations. Stripped of the actual letters, the words remain as only an echo of the informing system. The fifteen heroines are further revealed in a large-scale wall drawing with accompanying sound installation which layers incantatory murmurings taken from classical translations and a contemporary adaptation of Ovid’s epistolary poems. Ideas of language, voice, and story continue to unfold throughout the gallery in various forms, including silkscreen prints, mirrored objects, paintings, and a levitating, triangular bronze Penelope sculpture. Join us at the gallery Saturday, September 12th, at 2:30 pm for an artist talk with Victoria Haven and author Claire Dederer discussing the process surrounding this body of work and how it connects to ideas of perception, voice and language in her artist practice.
events.title: THE HEROINES · Victoria Haven

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

Through conversation, live demonstrations, and audience Q&A, discover the traditions, symbolism, and training behind this timeless practice. What is Pukulan? Pukulan is a style of the Indonesian martial art known as Silat. The name Pukulan comes from the Indonesian word “to strike” and means “a series of blows with returning hands and feet.” Pukulan practitioners throw rapid, whip-style strikes out of flowing movement derived from four animal styles: monkey, tiger, crane, and snake. These traditional styles were born from a time when practitioners found strength in a connection with the natural world by embracing animal movements. events.summary: Last Thursday Artist Reception August 27, 6 to 9pm. Show Dates: August 27 through September 21. Outside City Limits Forget the commute. Turn the car around! Leave civilization behind and delight in the fused-glass landscapes of Linda Gerrard and wander through the threaded tree paintings of Michelle L. Purvis instead. Michelle’s lifelong fascination with trees, mountains, and how they relate to humans strongly influences her art. In this series of framed acrylic paintings on paper, each work is a portrait of a specific tree, dressed in embroidered finery to fit its personality. She made their acquaintance and sketched them from life while she was camping or on vacation. While they may have been created completely in her studio, Linda’s fused-glass landscapes evoke a real sense of natural place. Starting with a base sheet of glass, she builds her images by arranging and kiln-firing layer after layer of colored glass, often leaving lovely textured details on the surface. Linda and Michelle, two long-time members of the gallery, invite you to take in the vistas of meadow, marsh and mountainside, to reach out to stroke the colorful bark of the trees or a heron’s plumage, and to discover what lies just Outside City Limits. Showing in the front windows of Alberta Street Gallery. Alberta Street Gallery is a cooperative gallery of 30 local artists in the heart of the Alberta Arts District in Northeast Portland. In addition to our members’ art, we mount monthly shows that begin on the “Last Thursday” of every month. Our front windows feature new work by two of our member artists, and we curate group shows in Lavaun's Community Gallery, a special exhibition space inside the gallery named for and made possible by gallery member Lavaun Benavidez Heaster, a legally blind collage artist who died in 2020.

events.summary: More than 40 leading local architecture firms present the best designs they hoped to build but that didn’t come to pass. Projects will include Allied Works’ elegant proposal commissioned by the New York Metropolitan Museum for its Modern and Contemporary Art Wing, West of West’s concept studies for infill housing in Los Angeles and Portland, Henneberry Eddy’s adaptive reuse of the recently destroyed Centennial Mills, and many more. In addition, the exhibition offers visions from Portland’s past, from Edward Bennett’s 1932 plan to reenvision Portland in the City Beautiful movement to Skidmore Owings Merrill’s “Delta Dome,” a 40,000-seat stadium in Delta Park, to GGN’s radical re-envisioning of Mt Tabor Park. It's a survey of Portland's past ambitions and its current array of design talent!
events.title: Unseen Portland Architecture: the best of Portland design. Never built

events.summary: Stringing Beads / Ensartar Cuentas brings together the work of Orquidia Violeta, Mariela Finvarb, Beatriz Bellorín, and Marisol Valencia in an exhibition that grew from the relationships formed during and after the 2024 Stelo Summer Invitational Residency. Expanded through a year of virtual gatherings, the exhibition reflects on how artistic dialogue continues to shape creative practice beyond the residency itself. Through photography, video, textiles, ceramics, painting, and installation, the artists explore migration, identity, memory, grief, ecology, ancestral knowledge, and care. Like beads threaded together, each work retains its individuality while contributing to a larger conversation about belonging, transformation, and the enduring connections forged through shared experience. The lion dance \(Wǔshi, 舞獅\) is one of the oldest and most recognizable traditions in Chinese culture. Combining martial arts, music, dance, storytelling, and craftsmanship, it has been performed for more than 1,000 years to celebrate important milestones and bring communities together. Their mission is to preserve and promote traditional performing arts through dynamic entertainment that resonates with every generation. As the largest dragon and lion dance team in Oregon, they proudly offer vibrant and captivating performances across the Pacific Northwest. events.summary: Raised in England, Hynes started out as a teenage punk in the UK band Test Icicles before releasing two orchestral acoustic pop records as Lightspeed Champion. In 2011, he released Coastal Grooves, the first of four solo albums under themonikerBlood Orange. His album, Freetown Sound, was released to critical acclaim in 2016, and saw Hynes defined as one of the foremost musical voices of his time, receiving comparisons to the likes of Kendrick Lamar and D'Angelo for his own searing and soothing personal document of life as a black man in America. He has collaborated with Solange, Skepta, FKA twigs, Carly Rae Jepsen, A$AP Rocky, Charlotte Gainsbourg, Blondie, and many other artists, and was recently one of four artists invited to the Kennedy Center to perform alongside Philip Glass. In addition to his production work, he scored the film Palo Alto, directed by Gia Coppola. Negro Swan was written and produced by Hynes. Says Hynes: "My newest album is an exploration into my own and many types of black depression, an honest look at the corners of black existence, and the ongoing anxieties of queer/people of color. A reach back into childhood and modern traumas, and the things we do to get through it all. The underlying thread through each piece on the album is the idea of HOPE, and the lights we can try to turn on within ourselves with a hopefully positive outcome of helping others out of their darkness
events.title: Blood Orange

events.summary: Run Time: 80 min. TICKETS $25 Doors 6:30 p.m.; Event 7 p.m. Select Showtime to Purchase Tickets Click here to learn more about accessibility at the Tomorrow Theater. THE EXPERIENCE: A Portland ENCORE screening of the 1926 Japanese Avant-Garde Experimental Film A PAGE OF MADNESS \(KURRUTTA ICHIPEIGI\) Directed by Teinosuke Kinugasa featuring a special live soundtrack performed by QUASI and SOFT RUMBLE \(Kathy Foster & Rachel Blumberg\). ON SCREEN: A Page of Madness 1926. Directed by Teinosuke Kinugasa. Runtime: 73 minutes. Lostfor 45 years until it was rediscovered by Kinugasa in his storehouse in 1971, the film is the product of anavant-gardegroup of artists in Japan known as the Shinkankakuha \(or School of New Perceptions\) who tried to overcomenaturalistic representation. The film is set in a mental institution in contemporary Japan and revolves around a man who takes a janitorial job at the institution after his wife is taken in as a patient there. Eventually, the janitor himself begins to slip into a fantasy world in his own mind, while the pain and suffering continue around him. Using superimpositions, rapid and insistent visual patterns, fantasy sequences, and the visual flamboyance of actors impersonating mad people, A Page of Madness builds an atmosphere of astonishing intensity. ON STAGE: QUASI \(Performers\) - Quasi was formed in 1993 by Janet Weiss and Sam Coomes, in Portland Oregon. Since then, the band has toured the world \(more or less\) however many times, and released a number of well-regarded albums on several of the most respected American indie labels, including Up, Touch and Go, Kill Rock Stars, and Sub Pop, and internationally with longtime comrades Domino Records. Concurrently, JW was a longtime member of Sleater-Kinney, as well as recording and/or touring with Courtney Barnett and Kurt Vile, Stephen Malkmus and the Jicks, Bright Eyes, the Shins, Elliott Smith, the Go-Betweens, and others, and is currently also a member of Portland band Slang. SC has worked with Elliott Smith, Built to Spill, Jandek, the Go-Betweens, and others, and has toured and recorded as a solo artist. He is also currently a member of Jon Spencer and the HITmakers. Trivia!: Both Janet and Sam are two-time members of the Oregon Music Hall of Fame - JW for Quasi and Sleater-Kinney, and SC for Quasi and Heatmiser. Soft Rumble \(Performers\) - An exciting collaboration between two of Portland's most prolific musicians: Kathy Foster of Roseblood, Thermals, All Girl Summer Fun Band, Wooly Mountain, Hurry Up and Slang. And Rachel Blumberg of Field Drums, Arch Cape, M. Ward, The Decemberists and Michael Hurley. AUD
events.title: A Page of Madness (1926) with live score by Quasi and Soft Rumble

events.summary: Craig Robinson most notably portrayed acerbic Dunder-Mifflin employee Darryl Philbin on the Emmy-winning “The Office” on NBC. He is definitely a world away from his original career intentions; before deciding to pursue his comedy career full time, Robinson was a K-8 teacher in the Chicago Public School System. It was while he was studying education in Chicago that he also discovered his love of acting and comedy when he joined the famed Second City Theatre. As a stand-up comedian, Robinson first made his mark in the comedy circuit at the 1998 Montreal Just For Laughs Festival. That year, he also won the Oakland Comedy Festival Awards and the Miller Genuine Draft 1996 Comedy Search. He soon went on to perform his act on “The Jimmy Kimmel Show" and “Real Time with Bill Maher.” Now headlining venues and festivals across the country, he does both solo acts as well as full-band sets – “The Nasty Delicious” – tying together his lyrical comedy with his finesse at the piano. Whether Robinson shows up with just his keyboard or his seven-man band, the clubs are packed to the brim with raucous laughter and musical comedy. events.summary: Tillinghast Mountain creates unique America music with Appalachian and Idahoan influences. Their show involves harmonious guitar, cello, banjo, thoughtful songwriting, and usually a healthy dose of off-beat humor. "Richard Tillinghast is a poet; he has traveled America and abroad with his senses open and attuned and has distilled many thoughts, impressions and feelings into beautiful, restless verse in song." \(Dave Horner, Creative Loafing SC\). events.summary: What does it mean to lead, to worship, or to seek perfection — especially when the mirror keeps changing shape? In Take Me to Your Leader: The Seoul of a Clown, Corean-born, Pacific Northwest–based performance artist Monel Chang (aka Moldy Melon) dives headfirst into a kaleidoscopic exploration of beauty, power, and the absurd rituals of becoming. Part pansori opera, part clown confession, part K-beauty séance, this solo performance unfolds like a fever dream across three acts. We meet a traditional pansori singer, steeped in ancient song and wonder; a K-beauty devotee, consumed by an altar of serums, snails, and sheet masks; and a self-proclaimed dictator, leading a birthday party for themself with military precision and toddler rage. Each character teeters between the sacred and the ridiculous, revealing how rituals of transformation — whether spiritual, aesthetic, or political — can both liberate and imprison us. Through meticulous physicality, voice, and gesture, Chang conjures a world where skincare becomes salvation, laughter becomes resistance, and a dictator’s parade dissolves into a child’s tantrum. With cues of light, sound, and scent, the stage transforms into a surreal landscape of shifting identities — from vanity table to battlefield, from face mask to flag. At once hilarious and haunting, The Seoul of a Clown interrogates the myth of perfection — in beauty, in heritage, and in leadership — while celebrating the messy, clownish heart that beats beneath it all. Drawing from Korean folk traditions, contemporary clowning, and the heightened absurdity of global pop culture, Chang builds a world where the search for “flawless skin” mirrors the search for self, and where even dictators might cry under their makeup. The result is a sensorial and spiritual satire — a ritual of laughter, longing, and self-recognition. Whether you leave glowing, weeping, or simply moisturized, Take Me to Your Leader: The Seoul of a Clown promises an unforgettable night at the edge of comedy and catharsis.
events.title: Take Me To Your Leader: The Seoul of a Clown

events.summary: 7pm doors, 8pm show All ages welcome Madison Ryann Ward Faith-based singer/songwriter Madison Ryann Ward writes warmhearted songs that mix mature pop and contemporary R&B with accents of gospel, blues, and folk. Previously signed to Rick Rubin's American Recordings, for which she cut the secular Beyond Me EP \(2019\), she has established herself as an independent artist with her own Zelda House Records, issuing a slew of singles before making her full-length debut with A New Thing \(2023\), a bright showcase for her commanding and understated voice. Ward grew up in her native Oklahoma hearing a wide range of music. Her mother played piano in church, and she soaked up blues and soul classics while working in her teens at her father's restaurant. A year-round athletic star in high school, Ward excelled in volleyball at Oklahoma University with plans of going pro. Her path changed after an informal cafeteria recording of her singing Aretha Franklin's "Chain of Fools" went viral. This encouraged Ward to build an online following with regular uploads of covers, and she eventually devoted herself to developing her voice and budding songwriting talent, leading to a deal with producer Rick Rubin and his American Recordings label. After she made her commercial debut with the Rex Rideout collaboration "Mirror" in 2018, Ward continued the next year with Beyond Me, a four-track EP featuring the equally lean and soulful ballad "BRKN." Ward then went independent, and from 2020 through 2022 progressed with singles such as "Higher," "Player," "Love&Adoration," and "Anchor." In 2023, she delivered A New Thing, an album over an hour in length with a few of the preceding singles placed throughout the sequence. ~ Andy Kellman, Rovi

events.summary: Surgery always carries some level of risk, and not every unexpected outcome is the result of negligence. However, when a healthcare professional fails to meet the accepted standard of medical care and that failure causes avoidable harm, the situation may amount to Surgical Negligence. Determining the difference often requires a careful review of medical records, expert opinions, and the circumstances surrounding the procedure. Warning signs can include operating on the wrong site, delayed treatment of complications, retained surgical instruments, anesthesia errors, or inadequate post-operative care. It is also important to consider whether the patient was properly informed of the risks before consenting to surgery. Establishing negligence involves proving that the injury was preventable and directly caused by substandard care rather than an unavoidable complication. Because these cases can be medically and legally complex, professional legal guidance is essential. Ciano Carroll Solicitors represents individuals who believe they have suffered avoidable harm due to medical errors and helps them understand whether they may have a valid claim. Their experience in handling complex medical negligence matters enables clients to navigate the legal process with confidence. By working with independent medical experts and thoroughly investigating each case, the firm evaluates whether the required legal standard for negligence has been met. Anyone concerned about the outcome of a surgical procedure should seek advice as early as possible to protect their legal rights. Understanding the distinction between an accepted surgical risk and Surgical Negligence is the first step toward determining whether compensation may be available.
events.title: How can you tell if a surgical complication was actually negligence?

events.summary: The Multnomah Arts Center (MAC) in Portland, Oregon will open two new exhibitions in its Front and Center Galleries this August. tende·r·eprisal // futu·re·prise, a group exhibition of bronze works created by multiple artists through a collaborative process led by elijah jamal asani, will be featured in the Front Gallery. In the Center Gallery, large-scale wood sculptures by Philip A. Robinson Jr. will be paired with functional and sculptural ceramic works by Swapna Mukhopadhyay. Both exhibitions run August 7–September 12, 2026, with a joint reception on Thursday, August 20, from 6 to 8 p.m. elijah jamal asani, a Nigerian-American artist, convened an intergenerational group of regional Black artists to create a collection of contemporary bronze artifacts. Their work was made in response to the historic theft of the Benin Bronzes. “Dating back to the 13th century, artists from the Kingdom of Benin, which is in modern-day southern Nigeria, cast bronze into sacred altar pieces and vessels of ancestral memory,” says asani. “However, in 1897, thousands of these bronze artifacts were looted by British forces.” They have yet to be repatriated. As an act of “selfdetermined restitution,” asani worked with other Black artists to create new bronzes. MAC is honored to exhibit eleven of these sculptures, created by Adriene Cruz, Midnite Seed Abioto, Intisar Abioto, Hanifah Abioto, Vaughn Kimmons, Turiya Raiah, Nyasiah Calixte, Lea Dry, Hannah Dry, Nawens Dry, and elijah jamal asani. Swapna Mukhopadhyay creates functional and sculptural porcelain works, all hand built. “The combination of aesthetics and functionality in handmade folk artifacts has always fascinated me,” she says. “My grandmother made traditional Bengali quilts (kanthas) and wove mats for sitting on the floor (asanas). I now realize how deeply I was influenced by watching her work.” Delicate drawn elements adorn many of her ceramic surfaces, and several recent works incorporate textiles and found objects. Mukhopadhyay describes her process as “improvising around what’s available,” informed by her longtime study of ethnomathematics. A retired PSU professor, she sees mathematics as inherent to creative practice and creative expression as integral to daily life across many cultures. Her ceramic pieces are often small in scale and characterized by what she calls their “putting togetherness.” Philip A. Robinson Jr. is a sculptor and conceptual artist whose work has been exhibited nationally and internationally. Working primarily in wood and metal, Robinson creates large-scale figurative and patterned works that explore memory, structure, and identity. “My practice examines structure as a living system—how materials carry memory, how patterns encode history, and how built environments shape identity,” he explains. “Whether in wood or steel, I am asking how structure holds memory—and how we locate ourselves within it.” The exhibition will include pieces from several bodies of work, including a 42” x 61” sculpture from Welcome In, which examines belonging, and several works from The House of Regina, which honor the legacy of his late mother, Dr. Regina Arnold. Robinson holds a BFA in Studio Art from Skidmore College and an MFA in Sculpture from the Mason Gross School of the Arts at Rutgers University. The Multnomah Arts Center is located at 7688 SW Capitol Hwy, Portland, OR, 97219. It is open Monday – Thursday 9 a.m. to 9:30 p.m., and Friday – Saturday 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. The galleries are free and open to the public during these hours. Additional Information: The Multnomah Arts Center is a part of Portland Parks & Recreation. MAC offers programs in a wide range of visual, music, movement, theater, and literary arts at an affordable cost to people of all ages. In addition to this vibrant arts education program, MAC runs a community-based visual arts exhibition program, which includes the MAC Front & Center Galleries. MAC also hosts theatre, music and dance performances, and other special events. The Multnomah Arts Center Association (MACA) is an all-volunteer, 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization that exists to support equity and access to arts education at MAC. MACA provides scholarships, supports community engagements efforts, and provides specialized arts equipment and facility improvements. Their efforts expand opportunities and enhance the experience of students, instructors, and the community at-large. For more information about MAC or MACA, please call 503.823.2787 or visit www.multnomahartscenter.org
events.title: Bronze, Wood, and Clay Contemporary Sculpture Exhibitions at MAC

events.summary: PDX CONTEMPORARY ART is pleased to present THE HEROINES, a new exhibition by Seattle-based artist Victoria Haven. For this body of work, Victoria Haven referenced The Heroides, a collection of poems by Ovid written from the perspective of fifteen heroines of Greek and Roman mythology. Using the poems as source material and framework, the works in the exhibition dissect and reassemble mythological narratives into an invented language. The Heroines Alphabet, a series of graphite drawings, uses the title of the show as a system for revealing hidden words. Placed in a grid, Haven connects adjacent letters in ‘The Heroines’ to form new words, some with multiple readings or meanings. The Linguistic Architecture drawings abstract the alphabet further, transforming each letter of the title phrase into dark, inky rectangles with bright scarlet notations. Stripped of the actual letters, the words remain as only an echo of the informing system. The fifteen heroines are further revealed in a large-scale wall drawing with accompanying sound installation which layers incantatory murmurings taken from classical translations and a contemporary adaptation of Ovid’s epistolary poems. Ideas of language, voice, and story continue to unfold throughout the gallery in various forms, including silkscreen prints, mirrored objects, paintings, and a levitating, triangular bronze Penelope sculpture. Join us at the gallery Saturday, September 12th, at 2:30 pm for an artist talk with Victoria Haven and author Claire Dederer discussing the process surrounding this body of work and how it connects to ideas of perception, voice and language in her artist practice.
events.title: THE HEROINES · Victoria Haven

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: Last Thursday Artist Reception August 27, 6 to 9pm. Show Dates: August 27 through September 21. Forged & Fired: Art by Flame Fire is one of humanity’s oldest tools for transformation. From forged steel and kiln-fired clay to molten silver and sculpted wax, heat is the catalyst that turns raw elements into striking fine art. Curated by Alberta Street Gallery member Leslie McMillan, this invitational exhibition features six artists—Larry Holt, Bobby Pedersen, Cindy Caufman, John Hyland, Diane Moskowitz, and Ann Coskey—who harness extreme temperatures to bend raw materials to their vision. events.summary: Last Thursday Artist Reception August 27, 6 to 9pm. Show Dates: August 27 through September 21. Outside City Limits Forget the commute. Turn the car around! Leave civilization behind and delight in the fused-glass landscapes of Linda Gerrard and wander through the threaded tree paintings of Michelle L. Purvis instead. Michelle’s lifelong fascination with trees, mountains, and how they relate to humans strongly influences her art. In this series of framed acrylic paintings on paper, each work is a portrait of a specific tree, dressed in embroidered finery to fit its personality. She made their acquaintance and sketched them from life while she was camping or on vacation. While they may have been created completely in her studio, Linda’s fused-glass landscapes evoke a real sense of natural place. Starting with a base sheet of glass, she builds her images by arranging and kiln-firing layer after layer of colored glass, often leaving lovely textured details on the surface. Linda and Michelle, two long-time members of the gallery, invite you to take in the vistas of meadow, marsh and mountainside, to reach out to stroke the colorful bark of the trees or a heron’s plumage, and to discover what lies just Outside City Limits. Showing in the front windows of Alberta Street Gallery. Alberta Street Gallery is a cooperative gallery of 30 local artists in the heart of the Alberta Arts District in Northeast Portland. In addition to our members’ art, we mount monthly shows that begin on the “Last Thursday” of every month. Expanded through a year of virtual gatherings, the exhibition reflects on how artistic dialogue continues to shape creative practice beyond the residency itself. Through photography, video, textiles, ceramics, painting, and installation, the artists explore migration, identity, memory, grief, ecology, ancestral knowledge, and care. In addition, the exhibition offers visions from Portland’s past, from Edward Bennett’s 1932 plan to reenvision Portland in the City Beautiful movement to Skidmore Owings Merrill’s “Delta Dome,” a 40,000-seat stadium in Delta Park, to GGN’s radical re-envisioning of Mt Tabor Park. It's a survey of Portland's past ambitions and its current array of design talent!

events.summary: Sunday, Aug. 30 & Saturday, Sept. 5 | 2:00 PM | Free with admission or membership Summary Tickets Parking Experience Overview Join members of Many Roads Martial Arts as they demonstrate various specialties, such as Shaolin Kung Fu and Kali — a weapons-based Filipino style of martial arts. Watch in wonder as they punch, kick, and move with precision! About the Performers Participation in this demo may vary. Jenny Lohr, Owner/Instructor Jenny has been practicing Shaolin Kung Fu and Tai Chi since 2005. As the owner of Many Roads Martial Arts Center, her focus is nurturing a supportive and safe learning environment while challenging everyone to keep growing and improving. Jenny loves the physical and mental challenges of martial arts and is very excited to share them with the students and instructors at the center. Jay Twitchell, Instructor Jay has studied various martial arts systems including boxing, wrestling, judo, karate, taekwondo, aikido, hopkido, kumdo, and muay thai kick boxing since he was 10. In other words, he has been used as a punching bag for over 30 years by masters and lifelong practitioners of these systems. His lifetime of experience getting kicked, punched, choked, kneed, elbowed, and thrown are invaluable in teaching others how not to be. Balancing his martial studies, Jay has 20 years of experience as a massage therapist and movement specialist, offering him a deep knowledge of the human body and healthy practice. Myk Olsen, Instructor Myk has been a Tai Chi Chuan practitioner since 1997 and has been teaching since 2013. His primary teachers were Gao Jamin and Yu Shaowen. Over the years, Myk has learned a multitude of forms in Yang, Chen, Wu, and Sun styles—both open-hand and weapons \(straight sword, broadsword, staff, spear, cane, deerhorn knives, and daggers\). While he used to compete in both forms and Push-Hands, Myk now focuses more time on teaching. His teaching style is student-centered and is focused on achieving a balance between the meditative and martial aspects of the forms. Myk also teaches a Tai Chi class specifically geared toward those with mobility and balance issues on Sunday afternoon. Joel, Instructor A lifetime student of martial arts, Joel has been training Shaolin Kung Fu and Tai Chi since 1999 and teaching since 2009. His teaching goal is to provide tools to improve every student’s physical, mental, and emotional health in a supportive, encouraging learning environment. Joel’s primary teaching focus is Chen Tai Chi as taught by Master George Xu \(Xu Guo Ming\). He also teaches our black belt Shaolin curriculum, Yang style Tai Chi, and 5 Element Qi Gong. events.summary: Portland, clear the afternoon. Phuture Phunk is taking over the White Owl Social Club patio for seven hours of bass, color, tropical heat, spacey sounds, and seriously funky grooves. DJ Spun brings decades of dancefloor experience from San Francisco to New York, joined by DJ Dazy, Funkhouser, and Kepi for a lineup built to keep things moving from the first record to the final beat. Saturday, September 5 2 PM–9 PM White Owl Social Club 1305 SE 8th Ave, Portland 21+ $13 presale | $20 at the door Come early, bring your people, and step into the Phuture Phunk. ARTIST SPOTLIGHT: DJ SPUN Raised on Bay Area punk, hip-hop, disco, house, acid, and the early San Francisco rave scene, DJ Spun has never stayed inside one musical lane. He began DJing in the late 1980s before becoming a major presence in New York’s underground dance community. Along the way, he founded Rong Music, helped bring disco edits to new generations of American dancefloors, and spent seven years curating music for MoMA PS1’s Warm Up series. Expect a set shaped by decades of digging, editing, experimenting, and knowing exactly when to take the dancefloor somewhere unexpected. ARTIST SPOTLIGHT: DJ DAZY DJ Dazy is a Los Angeles-based house DJ known for her deep, soulful, and funky sound, rooted in a lifelong connection to vinyl culture. She began DJing in 1991, often as the only female DJ in her scene, and went on to help shape West Coast house music through the 90s and early 2000s, including founding the female DJ collective Sister DJs. With over three decades behind the decks, her style is defined by warm basslines, musical storytelling, and an intuitive ability to read a dance floor. Whether opening a room or taking it deeper into the night, she creates a journey that feels both effortless and intentional. After stepping back for a period, DJ Dazy returned to the scene in 2024 with a renewed energy, blending her original vinyl roots with a modern digital setup. Since then, she has been actively playing across Los Angeles and beyond, sharing lineups with respected artists and reconnecting with the community that shaped her. Her sets move between deep house, soulful grooves, disco influences, and classic cuts from her extensive record collection, always focused on feeling over hype. Equally comfortable on vinyl or digital, she brings a level of experience and authenticity that comes from decades of dedication to the craft.
events.title: M IS FOR MUZIK Presents PHUTURE PHUNK w/ SPUN & DJ DAZY

The lion dance \(Wǔshi, 舞獅\) is one of the oldest and most recognizable traditions in Chinese culture. Combining martial arts, music, dance, storytelling, and craftsmanship, it has been performed for more than 1,000 years to celebrate important milestones and bring communities together. Their mission is to preserve and promote traditional performing arts through dynamic entertainment that resonates with every generation. As the largest dragon and lion dance team in Oregon, they proudly offer vibrant and captivating performances across the Pacific Northwest. events.summary: Founded in 2025 by award-winning classical guitar virtuoso and Artistic Director, Tye Austin, M.M., Wilder Frets: Classical Guitar in the Wilderness is a fiscally sponsored nonprofit concert series presenting open-air classical guitar concerts staged in the wilderness of the Pacific Northwest. From August 1 through October 1, Oregon native Tye Austin will perform more than 30 intimate outdoor concerts across 15 of Oregon's most breathtaking state parks—from coastal bluffs to old-growth forests, red rock canyons, thundering waterfalls, vineyards, and ranches. Audiences will experience world-class live music performances through our signature Wilder Sound wireless headphone technology, allowing every guest to enjoy crystal-clear audio while remaining immersed in the beauty of the natural world up to a 1/4 mile radius from the stage. Wilder Frets is more than a concert series. It is a community movement dedicated to making exceptional live music concerts and masterclasses accessible to everyone. Every ticket purchased helps support our growing community initiatives, including: Fret Not Tickets Program, providing complimentary concert tickets to individuals and families facing financial barriers. The Free Frets Initiative, donating free classical guitars, free masterclasses, and mentorship to at-risk from rural, tribal, and urban communities throughout Oregon. Our inaugural season has been made possible through the generosity of our season sponsors and community partners such as Heartbeat Silent Disco, Community Beats, Willamette Valley Music Company, the Maslow Project, and Oregon State Parks who believe that arts, education, conservation, and public access belong together. Whether you're an experienced concertgoer, an outdoor adventurer, or simply looking for a meaningful way to spend an evening, Wilder Frets offers an unforgettable experience unlike anything else in the Pacific Northwest. Join us this season and discover why music sounds even more extraordinary in the great outdoors. View complete tour schedule and purchase tickets online only at www.wilderfrets.org/tour
events.title: Wilder Frets: Classical Guitar in the Wilderness - Inaugural Concert Season

events.summary: What does it mean to lead, to worship, or to seek perfection — especially when the mirror keeps changing shape? In Take Me to Your Leader: The Seoul of a Clown, Corean-born, Pacific Northwest–based performance artist Monel Chang (aka Moldy Melon) dives headfirst into a kaleidoscopic exploration of beauty, power, and the absurd rituals of becoming. Part pansori opera, part clown confession, part K-beauty séance, this solo performance unfolds like a fever dream across three acts. We meet a traditional pansori singer, steeped in ancient song and wonder; a K-beauty devotee, consumed by an altar of serums, snails, and sheet masks; and a self-proclaimed dictator, leading a birthday party for themself with military precision and toddler rage. Each character teeters between the sacred and the ridiculous, revealing how rituals of transformation — whether spiritual, aesthetic, or political — can both liberate and imprison us. Through meticulous physicality, voice, and gesture, Chang conjures a world where skincare becomes salvation, laughter becomes resistance, and a dictator’s parade dissolves into a child’s tantrum. With cues of light, sound, and scent, the stage transforms into a surreal landscape of shifting identities — from vanity table to battlefield, from face mask to flag. At once hilarious and haunting, The Seoul of a Clown interrogates the myth of perfection — in beauty, in heritage, and in leadership — while celebrating the messy, clownish heart that beats beneath it all. Drawing from Korean folk traditions, contemporary clowning, and the heightened absurdity of global pop culture, Chang builds a world where the search for “flawless skin” mirrors the search for self, and where even dictators might cry under their makeup. The result is a sensorial and spiritual satire — a ritual of laughter, longing, and self-recognition. Whether you leave glowing, weeping, or simply moisturized, Take Me to Your Leader: The Seoul of a Clown promises an unforgettable night at the edge of comedy and catharsis.
events.title: Take Me To Your Leader: The Seoul of a Clown

events.summary: Balkan Bump is the global electronic music project orchestrated by trumpet player, producer and ethnomusicologist Will Magid. Balkan Bump’s music fuses heavy electronic production with global music influences including traditional Balkan brass melodies, Middle Eastern sounds and American hip hop. The Balkan Bump live show highlights Magid’s expertise as an orchestrator, ranging in size from a solo performer to a 12-piece band featuring a menagerie of global instruments including sitar, saz, oud, clarinet and trumpet. The live performance’s popularity has brought the project to global renown with performances at the world’s biggest music stages including Coachella, Bonnaroo and Lightning In A Bottle, as well as beloved jazz, blues and world music festivals including Harvest Music Festival and CA WorldFest, and numerous appearances at Colorado’s famed Red Rocks Amphitheatre. Balkan Bump debuted with the single “Aymo” alongside famed Slovenian producer Gramatik and American hip hop royalty Talib Kweli. Gramatik quickly championed the new project, unveiling Balkan Bump's live show on his Re:Coil Tour and releasing Balkan Bump’s debut EP on his Lowtemp label imprint. Since then the Balkan Bump project has gone on to collaborate with global and live music projects Beats Antique and Moon Hooch; international electronic music superstars CloZee, Fakear, & Manic Focus; and American hip hop icon The Gift Of Gab (Blackalicious). Balkan Bump has been featured in Billboard Magazine, NPR’s The World, The San Francisco Chronicle and Magnetic Magazine. In 2020 Magid curated a series of global music mixes for Los Angeles-based Dublab Radio under the Balkan Bump alias. As a solo artist, Will Magid has collaborated and performed with artists including Bonobo, Erykah Badu, Pretty Lights, and soul music legend Solomon Burke. He has led numerous jazz and global music outfits including his eponymous soul-funk band’s seminal Alligator Spacewalk album in 2016, and the 2017 neoclassical exploration Lunar Conquest Suite. His music has been featured in campaigns for global brands including Warner Brothers, Uber, Porsche, HP, Vogue, GoPro and Ubisoft. Magid graduated from The UCLA Herb Alpert School of Music with a degree in Ethnomusicology.

events.summary: TICKETS truewest.info/WITCH26 On Sale Friday, June 5 at 10am PT This Event is All Ages ---------------------------------------- A pioneering Zambian psychedelic act, W.I.T.C.H. \(the name is an acronym, standing for We Intend to Cause Havoc\) were one of the defining acts of Zamrock, a fusion of Western rock and rhythm & blues with traditional African sounds. They were among Zambia's most popular and influential bands in the 1970s as a wave of psychedelic and hard rock gained an audience in Africa. A landlocked nation in the South of Africa, Zambia was formerly Northern Rhodesia until gaining its independence in 1964, and as Zambia established its own national identity, local musicians began embracing the progressive influences of artists such as the Beatles, the Rolling Stones, and Jimi Hendrix, as well as the forward-thinking soul and funk sounds of James Brown. By the mid-'70s, Zambia was falling into political chaos as the nation's once-profitable mining industry ran dry, and many Zamrock bands reflected this with a darker, more psychedelic influenced sound that suggested a familiarity with the likes of Deep Purple and Grand Funk Railroad. W.I.T.C.H.'s 1972 debut, Introduction, was the first commercial album released by a Zambian band, and they continued to deliver music until fading into dormancy in the mid-'80s. A reissue campaign launched in 2011 brought the band to a new generation of listeners, and W.I.T.C.H. reunited in 2014 and started touring again shortly thereafter. In 2023, they released Zango, their first new album in almost 40 years. The original lineup of W.I.T.C.H. included vocalist Emanyeo "Jagari" Chanda, guitarists Chris Mbewe and John Muma, bassist Gedeon Mulenga, and drummer Boidi Sinkala, who were veterans of Zambian cover bands of the late '60s; Chanda \(whose nickname "Jagari" came from his fascination with Mick Jagger, one of his strongest influences\) had worked with the Red Balloons and the Boyfriends \(the latter group would evolve into another key Zamrock outfit, Peace\), while most of the other members were members of Kingston Market. . Fuelled by marijuana and Western rock and soul, the group's debut album, Introduction, was released in 1972, and was among the first commercially released LPs issued in Zambia. W.I.T.C.H.'s third album, 1975's Lazy Bones!!, is generally regarded as their finest work; while they were hampered by the primitive recording technology available in Africa, they developed a large following in Zambia and were playing stadium-sized shows throughout the continent. In the 21st century, crate diggers interested in idiosyncratic rock sounds from around the world rediscovered W.I.T.C.H., and the German reissue label Shadoks released new CD editions of Introduction and Lazy Bones!! In 2011 the American label Now Again Records released We Intend to Cause Havoc!, a comprehensive W.I.T.C.H. box set that featured their five studio albums plus a bonus collection of single tracks and unreleased material. This sparked new interest in the band, and by 2013, a Chanda-led W.I.T.C.H. with Mwondela, had regrouped and was touring again. In 2023, W.I.T.C.H. released Zango, their first album of new material in almost 40 years. It included contributions from fellow Zambian artists such as Sampa the Great . In June 2025, they released Sogolo, their second album. ~Mark Deming, Rovi

events.summary: From her breakthrough 2019 self-titled mixtape to her 2021 debut Troubled Paradise and 2023’s STARFUCKER, SLAYYYTER proved herself to be one of the great shape-shifters of our time, taking the past, present, and future of pop and twisting it to her will. Early successes — “Daddy AF” went from viral hit making SLAYYYTER’s name online to soundtracking a key scene in the Oscar Best Picture winner Anora — fueled accolades from publications including Billboard, Paper, Variety, Rolling Stone, Pitchfork, and more, while earning SLAYYYTER opening slots with forebears like Tove Lo and Kesha. But even with all that, SLAYYYTER decided something wasn’t quite right. She decided to become who she was all along, underneath it all: the WOR$T GIRL IN AMERICA. SLAYYYTER’s third album is the most authentically her, while also boasting her most fully realized creative direction yet. She revisited her upbringing in St. Louis, and decided to make “iPod music” — a free-for-all of feral punk, corroded pop, and raunchy rap — conjuring the “Midwest-core tweaker bar rat” characters of her youth. Early singles “BEAT UP CHANEL$,” “CANNIBALISM!,” and “CRANK” steadily built hype for the project over the course of 2025, with fans fervently embracing the raw, swaggering Slayyyter that emerged from the ashes of her past selves. WOR$T GIRL IN AMERICA is both revelation and evolution, killing the SLAYYYTER we thought we knew so SLAYYYTER could be born for real.
events.title: Slayyyter & Pearly Drops

The band \(Rick Miller – guitar and vocals, Mary Huff – bass and vocals, Dave Hartman – drums\) has been playing together for over 30 years. Their musical journey has taken them from all-night North Carolina house parties to late night TV talk shows \(Conan O’Brien, The Tonight Show\), from performing at the base of Mt. Fuji in Japan to rockin’ out for the inmates at North Carolina correctional facilities. They’ve shared a stage with many musical luminaries including Link Wray, Loretta Lynn, Hasil Adkins and Patti Smith. Their music has been featured in movies and TV, parodied by Weird Al, and used to sell everything from diamonds to pork sausage. In 2014 the band was honored by the Southern Folklife Collection at the University of North Carolina Chapel Hill with an exhibition featuring their music and cultural contributions. Their legendary live shows are a testament to the therapeutic powers of foot-stomping, butt-shaking rock and roll and what Rolling Stone dubbed “a hell raising rock and roll party.” At Home with Southern Culture on the Skids is the latest full length album from the band and was released in March of 2021. It was recorded during the stay at home period of the pandemic when the band was at home and not touring. The album consists of 11 tracks recorded and mixed in Rick Miller’s living room with some additional tracks recorded at his studio, The Kudzu Ranch. The first radio single off the album is “Run Baby Run”—a rocking number with deep garage roots. SCOTS bassist Mary Huff provides an urgent vocal while the band pulls back the throttle on a full race fuzz fest—cause she’s gotta to go fast! Run Baby Run! The other songs on the album are a combination of the band’s unique mix of musical genres: rock and roll, surf, folk and country—all a bit off-center, what Rick proudly calls “our wobbly Americana”. Rick goes on, “We put a few more acoustic guitars on this one, as you would expect if you recorded in your living room, but it still rocks like SCOTS. So put your headphones on, get in your favorite chair/sofa/recliner, put on “At Home With” and let’s hang out for a while.”
events.title: Southern Culture on the Skids

This Event is All Ages ---------------------------------------- Portland indie-rock stalwarts The Weather Machine return home this spring to celebrate the release of their fifth studio record, Love & Science Fiction, with a special hometown performance at the Aladdin Theater on May 23 rd . Recorded in Sellwood with producer Gus Berry, the album brings together the band’s signature lyrical intelligence and lush, adventurous sound. Love & Science Fiction was written by frontman Slater Smith after relocating to Wellington, New Zealand, where the songs took shape on nature walks and quiet evenings far from home. These new works are a deep and cozy exploration of spiritual bargaining, touching on themes of romance, gratitude, and letting go to examine how we use sometimes-treacherous but always-beautiful fantasies to navigate life. Over two weeks in Sellwood, Smith reunited with longtime collaborators Tim Karplus \(guitar \+ keys\), Luke Hoffman \(drums\), André Zapata \(bass\), and Noah Bernstein \(sax \+ clarinet\) to arrange and record what started out as voice memo lyrics and melodies stored on Smith's phone. The result is something special. Drawing inspiration from Joe Cocker, The Cranberries, and Andrew Bird, Love & Science Fiction feels nostalgic and modern, an album both whimsical and profound, and quintessentially Pacific Northwest. Rarely do The Weather Machine’s local members reunite in one place, making this Aladdin Theater performance a uniquely Portland moment and a celebration of enduring creative friendship. With Love & Science Fiction, the band delivers their most ambitious and heartfelt record to date – a work of imagination, gratitude, and coming home.

events.summary: Surgery always carries some level of risk, and not every unexpected outcome is the result of negligence. However, when a healthcare professional fails to meet the accepted standard of medical care and that failure causes avoidable harm, the situation may amount to Surgical Negligence. Determining the difference often requires a careful review of medical records, expert opinions, and the circumstances surrounding the procedure. Warning signs can include operating on the wrong site, delayed treatment of complications, retained surgical instruments, anesthesia errors, or inadequate post-operative care. It is also important to consider whether the patient was properly informed of the risks before consenting to surgery. Establishing negligence involves proving that the injury was preventable and directly caused by substandard care rather than an unavoidable complication. Because these cases can be medically and legally complex, professional legal guidance is essential. Ciano Carroll Solicitors represents individuals who believe they have suffered avoidable harm due to medical errors and helps them understand whether they may have a valid claim. Their experience in handling complex medical negligence matters enables clients to navigate the legal process with confidence. By working with independent medical experts and thoroughly investigating each case, the firm evaluates whether the required legal standard for negligence has been met. Anyone concerned about the outcome of a surgical procedure should seek advice as early as possible to protect their legal rights. Understanding the distinction between an accepted surgical risk and Surgical Negligence is the first step toward determining whether compensation may be available.
events.title: How can you tell if a surgical complication was actually negligence?

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: Last Thursday Artist Reception August 27, 6 to 9pm. Show Dates: August 27 through September 21. Outside City Limits Forget the commute. Turn the car around! Leave civilization behind and delight in the fused-glass landscapes of Linda Gerrard and wander through the threaded tree paintings of Michelle L. Purvis instead. Michelle’s lifelong fascination with trees, mountains, and how they relate to humans strongly influences her art. In this series of framed acrylic paintings on paper, each work is a portrait of a specific tree, dressed in embroidered finery to fit its personality. She made their acquaintance and sketched them from life while she was camping or on vacation. While they may have been created completely in her studio, Linda’s fused-glass landscapes evoke a real sense of natural place. Starting with a base sheet of glass, she builds her images by arranging and kiln-firing layer after layer of colored glass, often leaving lovely textured details on the surface. Linda and Michelle, two long-time members of the gallery, invite you to take in the vistas of meadow, marsh and mountainside, to reach out to stroke the colorful bark of the trees or a heron’s plumage, and to discover what lies just Outside City Limits. events.summary: Step into the magic of the forest with author Joeanally Gonzalez, who received a 2026-2027 Milagro Artist Fund grant to support this bilingual (Spanish & English) family-friendly celebration marking the dual-language release of her new bilingual children’s book, Nico the Banana Slug. Kicking off with a brief introduction, Gonzalez shares the heart behind the story, her love for our local ecosystem, and the inspiration behind the art. Attendees then watch the pages come to life in a dynamic, bilingual puppet show packed with interactive, dual-language fun for all fluency levels. The excitement continues with a hands-on creative workshop. While kids craft their very own paper puppets, parents can meet the author, chat about forest stewardship, and purchase personalized, signed copies of her book. Joeanally González is a multidisciplinary artist, educator, and cultural worker based in East Portland. Holding a BFA from the Puerto Rico School of Fine Arts and a Fashion Design Certificate from Centro Moda Lisa Thon, her career spans Puerto Rican theater, costume design at Walt Disney World®, and authoring the bilingual children’s book, Nico the Banana Slug. Since 2017, she has led vital bilingual community workshops across Oregon. Recognized with honors like RACC Grants, Joeanally’s vibrant exhibitions celebrate immigrant stories and ecological resilience, seamlessly bridging professional design with grass-roots activism. "Completely eye-opening for me, and for so many of us who make stories for a living." - Ira Glass "One of the best documentaries and one of the best comedies ever made." - Patton Oswalt ON SCREEN: Sherman's March 1985. Directed by Ross McElwee. Runtime: 2 hours 38 minutes. Armed with a 16mm camera and a grant to make a documentary about the lingering aftermath of William Tecumseh Sherman's 1864 march to the sea, Ross McElwee gets sidetracked. After his girlfriend breaks up with him, Ross shifts his attention from the historical to the personal, to the battlefield of modern love, and embarks on a sociological chronicle that documents the courting rites and rituals of the New South. A generous and humanistic portrait of several remarkable women that Ross meets along the way, Sherman's March sketches its characters with novelistic sensitivity: Pat, an aspiring actress with a yen for Burt Reynolds; Claudia, a roller-skating interior designer; Jackie, the activist whose anti-nuclear advocacy dovetails with Ross's deepest fears; and above all, Charleen Swansea, Ross's mentor and a one-woman Greek chorus of unsolicited romantic counsel. A landmark of first-person filmmaking that presaged everything from Michael Moore to reality TV, Sherman's March is now available in a new 4K restoration. UNORTHODOX DO

From August 1 through October 1, Oregon native Tye Austin will perform more than 30 intimate outdoor concerts across 15 of Oregon's most breathtaking state parks—from coastal bluffs to old-growth forests, red rock canyons, thundering waterfalls, vineyards, and ranches. Audiences will experience world-class live music performances through our signature Wilder Sound wireless headphone technology, allowing every guest to enjoy crystal-clear audio while remaining immersed in the beauty of the natural world up to a 1/4 mile radius from the stage. Wilder Frets is more than a concert series. It is a community movement dedicated to making exceptional live music concerts and masterclasses accessible to everyone. Every ticket purchased helps support our growing community initiatives, including: Fret Not Tickets Program, providing complimentary concert tickets to individuals and families facing financial barriers. The Free Frets Initiative, donating free classical guitars, free masterclasses, and mentorship to at-risk from rural, tribal, and urban communities throughout Oregon. Our inaugural season has been made possible through the generosity of our season sponsors and community partners such as Heartbeat Silent Disco, Community Beats, Willamette Valley Music Company, the Maslow Project, and Oregon State Parks who believe that arts, education, conservation, and public access belong together. Whether you're an experienced concertgoer, an outdoor adventurer, or simply looking for a meaningful way to spend an evening, Wilder Frets offers an unforgettable experience unlike anything else in the Pacific Northwest. events.summary: The Multnomah Arts Center (MAC) in Portland, Oregon will open two new exhibitions in its Front and Center Galleries this August. tende·r·eprisal // futu·re·prise, a group exhibition of bronze works created by multiple artists through a collaborative process led by elijah jamal asani, will be featured in the Front Gallery. In the Center Gallery, large-scale wood sculptures by Philip A. Robinson Jr. will be paired with functional and sculptural ceramic works by Swapna Mukhopadhyay. Both exhibitions run August 7–September 12, 2026, with a joint reception on Thursday, August 20, from 6 to 8 p.m. elijah jamal asani, a Nigerian-American artist, convened an intergenerational group of regional Black artists to create a collection of contemporary bronze artifacts. Their work was made in response to the historic theft of the Benin Bronzes. “Dating back to the 13th century, artists from the Kingdom of Benin, which is in modern-day southern Nigeria, cast bronze into sacred altar pieces and vessels of ancestral memory,” says asani. “However, in 1897, thousands of these bronze artifacts were looted by British forces.” They have yet to be repatriated. As an act of “selfdetermined restitution,” asani worked with other Black artists to create new bronzes. MAC is honored to exhibit eleven of these sculptures, created by Adriene Cruz, Midnite Seed Abioto, Intisar Abioto, Hanifah Abioto, Vaughn Kimmons, Turiya Raiah, Nyasiah Calixte, Lea Dry, Hannah Dry, Nawens Dry, and elijah jamal asani. Swapna Mukhopadhyay creates functional and sculptural porcelain works, all hand built. “The combination of aesthetics and functionality in handmade folk artifacts has always fascinated me,” she says. “My grandmother made traditional Bengali quilts (kanthas) and wove mats for sitting on the floor (asanas). I now realize how deeply I was influenced by watching her work.” Delicate drawn elements adorn many of her ceramic surfaces, and several recent works incorporate textiles and found objects. Mukhopadhyay describes her process as “improvising around what’s available,” informed by her longtime study of ethnomathematics. A retired PSU professor, she sees mathematics as inherent to creative practice and creative expression as integral to daily life across many cultures. Her ceramic pieces are often small in scale and characterized by what she calls their “putting togetherness.” Philip A. Robinson Jr. is a sculptor and conceptual artist whose work has been exhibited nationally and internationally. Working primarily in wood and metal, Robinson creates large-scale figurative and patterned works that explore memory, structure, and identity. “My practice examines structure as a living system—how materials carry memory, how patterns encode history, and how built environments shape identity,” he explains. “Whether in wood or steel, I am asking how structure holds memory—and how we locate ourselves within it.” The exhibition will include pieces from several bodies of work, including a 42” x 61” sculpture from Welcome In, which examines belonging, and several works from The House of Regina, which honor the legacy of his late mother, Dr. Regina Arnold. Robinson holds a BFA in Studio Art from Skidmore College and an MFA in Sculpture from the Mason Gross School of the Arts at Rutgers University. The Multnomah Arts Center is located at 7688 SW Capitol Hwy, Portland, OR, 97219. It is open Monday – Thursday 9 a.m. to 9:30 p.m., and Friday – Saturday 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. The galleries are free and open to the public during these hours. Additional Information: The Multnomah Arts Center is a part of Portland Parks & Recreation. MAC offers programs in a wide range of visual, music, movement, theater, and literary arts at an affordable cost to people of all ages. In addition to this vibrant arts education program, MAC runs a community-based visual arts exhibition program, which includes the MAC Front & Center Galleries. MAC also hosts theatre, music and dance performances, and other special events. The Multnomah Arts Center Association (MACA) is an all-volunteer, 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization that exists to support equity and access to arts education at MAC. MACA provides scholarships, supports community engagements efforts, and provides specialized arts equipment and facility improvements. Their efforts expand opportunities and enhance the experience of students, instructors, and the community at-large. For more information about MAC or MACA, please call 503.823.2787 or visit www.multnomahartscenter.org

events.summary: Last Thursday Artist Reception August 27, 6 to 9pm. Show Dates: August 27 through September 21. Outside City Limits Forget the commute. Turn the car around! Leave civilization behind and delight in the fused-glass landscapes of Linda Gerrard and wander through the threaded tree paintings of Michelle L. Purvis instead. Michelle’s lifelong fascination with trees, mountains, and how they relate to humans strongly influences her art. In this series of framed acrylic paintings on paper, each work is a portrait of a specific tree, dressed in embroidered finery to fit its personality. She made their acquaintance and sketched them from life while she was camping or on vacation. While they may have been created completely in her studio, Linda’s fused-glass landscapes evoke a real sense of natural place. Starting with a base sheet of glass, she builds her images by arranging and kiln-firing layer after layer of colored glass, often leaving lovely textured details on the surface. Linda and Michelle, two long-time members of the gallery, invite you to take in the vistas of meadow, marsh and mountainside, to reach out to stroke the colorful bark of the trees or a heron’s plumage, and to discover what lies just Outside City Limits.
